decisions.reason: As an organic line extension in a growing category that fits the firm's stated expansion path and existing capabilities, it is likely to meet a tolerable aspiration level, so a large firm with some slack would usually keep it unless sales clearly disappoint.

This product is another low-risk organic extension close to the core assortment, and absent clear evidence of underperformance, boundedly rational management would be inclined to continue it while using existing production and retail relationships.

Organic pepper-coated salami is still close to the established offer but somewhat more niche than basic sliced meats, so it faces a moderate drop risk, yet the firm would likely retain it if results are around aspiration and shelf presence supports the organic range.

The beef in teriyaki aspic looks like a more experimental deli-counter specialty, and if its performance fell short of aspiration the firm would be likely to reallocate resources back to stronger core products or other development projects.

Fennel-flavoured sliced salami is a narrower taste variant than the firm's mainstream premium deli products, so in a large established German meat processor it is more likely to be cut if demand remains below aspiration after an initial trial period.

Liver pâté with veal is very close to the firm's traditional competence base and should be relatively easy to support with existing know-how and facilities, making continued marketing likely unless performance is clearly weak.
